question: Should OpenClaw accept this deny-over-allow exec approval overlay as the native security policy shape, including the new openclaw.json and exec-approvals.json fields, gateway protocol schema, node-host behavior, and plugin SDK exposure?
rationale: The patch is a plausible core implementation, but it changes host-command security semantics and compatibility-sensitive persisted/API surfaces that automation should not approve as product direction.

options.title: Accept After Docs-Map Repair
options.body: Regenerate docs/docs_map.md, then have a maintainer/security owner explicitly accept the persisted policy, node-host semantics, and SDK exposure before merge.

options.title: Hide Or Narrow SDK/API Surface
options.body: Keep the runtime enforcement but remove or hide helper exports and any unsupported public surface before accepting the feature.

options.title: Pause For Broader Exec Policy Design
options.body: Hold the branch if maintainers want denylist mode, prompt-vs-hard-deny, path-deny, UI editing, and external policy-engine overlap designed together.

recommendation.title: Accept After Docs-Map Repair
recommendation.body: Regenerate docs/docs_map.md, then have a maintainer/security owner explicitly accept the persisted policy, node-host semantics, and SDK exposure before merge.
